deep.reconstruction:
The page proves that the dual of L_0(E,F) is L^1(F,E). Here E and F are Hilbert spaces. L_0(E,F) is the space of compact operators with the operator norm, i.e. the norm-closure of the finite-rank operators E'⊗F. L^1(F,E) is the trace class (Schatten class S_1), defined on the previous page through singular values.

(1) The pairing is (u,v) = Tr(vu). On finite-rank operators this is the familiar duality between E'⊗F and F'⊗E.

(2) The natural map L^1(F,E) → (L_0(E,F))' is an isometry. Write v in Schmidt form v = Σ λ_i \bar f_i⊗e_i. The test operator u = Σ \bar e_i⊗f_i (finite partial sums) has norm ≤ 1, and (u,v) = Σ λ_i = ||v||_1.

(3) The map is surjective. Let Φ be a continuous linear form on L_0(E,F). Then (x',y) ↦ Φ(x'⊗y) is a continuous bilinear form on E'×F, so it defines a bounded operator v: F → E with Φ(u) = Tr(vu) for finite-rank u, and |Tr(vu)| ≤ M||u||. It remains to show that v is trace class ('de Fredholm').

Grothendieck abandons a first attempt (crossed out) and instead uses polar decomposition: w = (vv*)^{1/2} ∈ L(E,E), with v = Ww and w = Vv, where W and V are partial isometries. This reduces the problem to the case F = E and w ≥ 0.

- w is compact. Otherwise some infinite-dimensional spectral subspace H, stable under w, would carry w as an invertible operator. Testing on finite-rank projections onto H would make Tr grow linearly in the rank, contradicting the bound M.
- So w = Σ ρ_i \bar f_i⊗e_i. Taking u = Σ e_i⊗f_i over finite partial sums gives Σ ρ_i ≤ M. Hence w, and therefore v = Ww, is trace class.

(4) The page ends with a sketch of a 'méthode hilbertienne' for the dual of L^∞(E,F), the bounded operators. A continuous linear form there restricts to a trace-class part v ∈ L^1(F,E) plus a 'partie singulière'. This is the decomposition of B(H)* into normal and singular functionals.

Purpose: establishing the Hilbert-space duality K* = S_1 (and S_1* = B), as the model case for the nuclear/integral operator dualities of the tensor-product theory Grothendieck was developing in 1953.
errors: Domain bookkeeping in the polar decomposition is loose. With w = (vv*)^{1/2} on E and v: F→E, one has v = w·W with W: F→E a partial isometry (equivalently v = W|v| with |v| = (v*v)^{1/2} on F). Writing 'v = Ww' with w ∈ L(E,E) does not compose correctly. Harmless.
The machine transcription puts λ_i inside the test operator u. To get an isometry, u must be Σ \bar e_i⊗f_i without the coefficients (or with unimodular phases).

ideas.what: The dual of the compact operators K(E,F) is the trace class S_1(F,E), via the pairing Tr(vu), and the identification is isometric.
ideas.usually_credited_to: Schatten and von Neumann (1946–48); Schatten, 'A theory of cross-spaces' (1950)
ideas.where_published: Grothendieck, Produits tensoriels topologiques et espaces nucléaires (Memoirs AMS 16, 1955), Hilbert-space case of nuclear/integral duality; also Résumé de la théorie métrique (1953/56)

ideas.what: Proof that the operator induced by a bounded functional is trace class: polar decomposition, compactness via spectral subspaces, then testing against partial Schmidt sums.
The dual of B(E,F) splits into a trace-class (normal) part and a singular part.
ideas.modern_name: Normal/singular decomposition of B(H)* (B(H)* = S_1 ⊕ K^⊥)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a careful personal derivation of the classical Schatten–von Neumann duality K* = S_1, with a brief remark on singular functionals on B(H). All of it was known by 1950 or soon after, and it is absorbed into Grothendieck's published tensor-product theory.
transcription_corrections: Line 1: 'Dual de L_0(E,F). Le dual est identifié algébriquement avec L^1(F,E)': the superscript on L(F,E) appears as L^{1} (possibly with a mark); this is consistent with the trace class.
Isometry step: the test operator is u = Σ_i \bar e_i ⊗ f_i (no λ_i), giving (u,v) = Σ λ_i.
'il suffit de montrer que v est de Fredholm, utilisant |Tr vu| ≤ M||u|| pour u ∈ E'⊗F' — the inserted 'pour u∈E'⊗F' replaces the struck-out 'u∈L(E,E)'.
Later lines read roughly 'on voit aisément que W = Vv [?] isométrie partielle ..., montrons que w est de Fredholm, donc v = Ww aussi (le cas où F=E)'.
'il existerait un sous-espace H ⊂ E stable par w, où w serait inversible, ce qui amène une contradiction'.
Near the end: 'Méthode hilbertienne'; and 'Si Φ est une forme linéaire continue sur L^∞(E,F), elle donne par restriction un v ∈ L^1(F,E), plus une partie singulière'.
